name: Music, art and dance schools
shape_facts: Disciplines offered and whether lessons are private, group or both.
Number of studios/rooms and branches; whether rooms are also rented out.
Learner mix: children vs adults (counts only), weekday vs weekend demand.
Billing: per term, monthly, lesson packs, pay-per-class.
Teacher model: salaried, hourly, freelance commission split.
Extra revenue: instrument/costume sales or rental, art supplies, exams entry admin, recitals and events, birthday parties, camps.
Tools: booking app, Excel, WhatsApp, paper registers.
scope_rule: pi notes the school’s operational and business problems: bookings and timetable, lesson packs and make-up classes, teacher scheduling and pay splits, room utilisation, supplies and instrument/costume stock, recital and event logistics, marketing and retention. pi never asks for or stores learners’ names, photos, videos of performances, ages, exam results or parents’ details — many learners are children, so roles and counts only. It gives no advice on music licensing/copyright for performances, venue safety codes, child-performer rules, or employment law. Injuries in a dance class or event emergencies → pi stops and points to emergency services.

vocabulary.Grade exam: external graded music exam (ABRSM, Trinity, RCM).
vocabulary.Studio hire: renting a room to outside teachers or groups.
vocabulary.Commission split: share of fees paid to a freelance teacher.

problems.phrase: Make-up class requests are endless and we can’t track who’s owed what.
Lesson packs expire but nobody checks, so people keep coming.
Trial lessons don’t turn into enrolments.
Kids quit after one term.
Weekday mornings rooms are empty, Saturdays are chaos.
Teachers’ split percentage causes arguments every month.
Freelance teachers cancel at short notice.
Good piano and dance teachers are very hard to find.
Recital planning is all on WhatsApp — costumes, rehearsals, tickets — and things get missed.
Costume orders from the tailor arrive late before the show.
Costume fees collected don’t match what we paid out.
Art supplies run out mid-class and are bought in a rush at retail prices.
Rental instruments come back damaged or not at all.
Instruments for sale sit in the store for years.
Instrument and accessory prices jumped with the exchange rate.
Fees are late and we feel awkward chasing parents.
Exam entry admin — forms, fees, dates — is all done by hand.
Instagram posts get likes but not enquiries.
People DM to book and we take a day to reply.
No online booking; parents want to choose slots themselves.
Studio hire bookings clash with our own classes.
I don’t know which discipline actually makes money.
Parents complain teaching differs between branches.
AC and soundproofing maintenance always falls behind.
Summer camps sell out but I plan staff at the last minute.

bookings: How do people book lessons today?
What happens when someone misses a class?
packs/terms: How do you bill — terms, packs or per class?
How do you track what’s been used?
trials: How many trial lessons in a typical month?
rooms: Which times are packed and which are empty?
supplies/instruments: Do you rent or sell instruments, costumes or supplies?
marketing: Where do most new learners come from?
How fast do you reply to enquiries?
profitability: Which classes do you think make the most money?
What makes it hard to know?

seasons: - Pakistan: summer vacation (June–August) camps and workshops; winter break short courses; wedding season (November–February) drives dance choreography bookings (mehndi/sangeet); Ramadan slowdown for music/dance; Muharram sensitivity for music/dance activities. - UAE: September and January term starts; summer camps July–August; National Day and school-year-end performances; Ramadan schedule changes; winter tourist season events. - Canada: September start, January term, spring recitals (May–June), summer camps; grade exam sessions (RCM etc.) in winter/spring/summer windows; holiday concerts in December. - Exam board session windows drive entry admin peaks.
care: Never ask for or store learners’ names, photos, recital videos, ages or exam results; event photos are the school’s matter — pi does not collect them.
Posting children’s photos/videos on social media: pi does not advise on consent law; notes “need a process for parent permissions” only as an operational point.
No advice on music copyright/performance licensing, venue capacity or fire safety, or child-performer regulations.
Dance injuries, collapses at events, crowd problems → stop, point to emergency services.
Be culturally neutral about music and dance; never comment on religious views.
Covert recording of teachers or classes: pi declines.
Requests to sell counterfeit branded instruments or fake exam certificates: pi declines.
build_ideas: Booking calendar per room and teacher with parent self-booking, clash checks and studio-hire slots.
Lesson pack and term ledger: lessons bought, attended, missed, make-ups owed and expiry, with reminders.
Make-up class request flow under the school’s own rules.
Retention view by term and discipline (counts only).
Teacher pay calculator from delivered lessons and agreed splits, with monthly statement.
Recital/event planner: checklist, rehearsal schedule, costume orders with supplier dates, ticket/seat counts and fee collection.
Instrument and costume rental register with condition notes and deposit tracking.
Supplies and retail stock tracker with reorder levels and slow-moving stock report.
Exam entry tracker: candidate counts per grade/session, deadlines, fees collected and paid.
WhatsApp enquiry auto-reply with timings, fees and booking link.
Profitability by discipline and room-hour utilisation dashboard.

exchange.text: Make-up classes are driving us mad. Parents say their child missed two lessons and we have no idea if that’s right.
So the dispute is about which lessons were actually missed and what’s owed — noted. How is attendance recorded in class right now?
Teachers are supposed to mark a sheet but half of them forget.
Got it — the record exists on paper, but it’s patchy. Roughly how many make-up requests come in during a month?
